In mathematics, a '''layer group''' is a three-dimensional extension of a [[wallpaper group]], with reflections in the third dimension. It is a [[space group]] with a two-dimensional lattice, meaning that it is symmetric over repeats in the two lattice directions. The symmetry group at each lattice point is an axial [[crystallographic point group]] with the main axis being perpendicular to the lattice plane.

Table of the 80 layer groups, organized by [[crystal system]] or lattice type, and by their point groups<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Kopsky |editor1-first=V. |editor2-last=Litvin |editor2-first=D.B. |title=International Tables for Crystallography, Volume E: Subperiodic Groups |url=http://it.iucr.org/E/ |publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] |location=Berlin, New York |edition=5th |isbn=978-1-4020-0715-6 |doi=10.1107/97809553602060000105 |year=2002 |volume=E}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hitzer |first1=E.S.M. |last2=Ichikawa |first2=D. |title=Representation of crystallographic subperiodic groups by geometric algebra |journal=Electronic Proc. of AGACSE |issue=3 |date=17–19 Aug 2008 |location=Leipzig, Germany |arxiv=1306.1280 |bibcode=2013arXiv1306.1280H}}</ref>
:

== Correspondence Between Layer Groups and Plane Groups ==
The surjective mapping from a layer group to a [[wallpaper group]] ([[plane group]]) can be obtained by disregarding symmetry elements along the stacking direction, typically denoted as the z-axis, and aligning the remaining elements with those of the [[plane group]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Sze|first=W.H.R.|last2=Xi|first2=B.|last3=Zhu|first3=J.|date=2025|title=Key difference of input data organization to the predictions of symmetry information and layer number for quasi-2D films from band structure|journal=Computational Condensed Matter|volume=42|article-number=e01009|doi=10.1016/j.cocom.2025.e01009|issn=2352-2143|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352214325000085|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The resulting surjective mapping provides a direct correspondence between layer groups and [[plane group]]s ([[wallpaper group]]s).
